asr.full_text: Hello everyone, welcome to the show around the Salama Developer Platform. My name is Catherine Gu, I'm the Head of Product for Digital Assets at the Salama Foundation. I'm here today with Itai from Dynamic. Thank you Itai for coming to our show and we're super excited to have you as well as FiveBlocks together as our first set of design partners. Maybe just start with telling us a little bit about yourself. What is Dynamecx and journey with Fireblocks? Yeah, absolutely. So thanks for having me. We're really excited about this. We're super thrilled to be a part of the initiative, so thanks for having us on. So a little bit just for folks that don't know, Dynamecx, which I co-founded has been acquired last year by Firebox. So now we're a part of the Firebox family. For anyone listening, dynamic. was a company that existed for about four years before we got acquired back by A. 16z in founders fund. What we did is essentially instilled to, is embed wall. So essentially when you log into MagicEden or to Crackin or to any of these platforms and you want a trade, a wallet is created for you, that wallet can be a custodial, I believe it's a custodial wallet or, uh, to any of these platforms and, um, you want to trade a wall that is created for you, that can be a custodial wallet, if it's an exchange or it can be a non custodial wallet, uh, if you own the keys as an end user. Uh, we generate those for, for developers at scale. We work with, again, the likes of a crack and MagicEden and many, many others. Uh, payroll companies like buyoclub, et cetera. And essentially we would give you the SDKs to generate those securely in a non-custodial way. Now that we're a part of Firebox, Firebox provides essentially the most comprehensive way to secure digital assets. Firebox does anywhere from tokenization to kind of powering internal treasury operations to powering giants like robinhood and revolut on all their trading operations and so um with dynamic being a part of firebox um you as a customer get kind of a full gamut of services anywhere from again on ramps and off ramps to tokenization to trading to everything in between in a single platform, whether you choose direct custody, self custody, qualified custodial, it's a unified platform that pretty much powers to our last check about 15% of all global stable coin movement globally. That's awesome. I think that yeah, it's super cool, the fact that now you guys are together as a single family. And I think there's a very rich set of key management experiences that an institution could think about down the road. And I think actually just building on that point, right? Because as you guys are working with us, for the launch of the Solana Developer Platform, and I think for the purpose of V1, it's a fairly minimum viable product. So it's a fairly straightforward kind of custodial kind of wallet management experience for the institutions. But I'm curious, as you're thinking about, and especially with everything you've seen, deal flows and stuff, as part of the Firelock sort of conversations, on the institutional use cases, what do you think is in the long term, combining these sort of embedded experience and custodial experience. What could be some, I guess, relatable use cases you can think about for institutions? Paul Olsen- Yeah, absolutely. So if you think about, so to your point, what we've seen when we work with remittance companies or payroll companies or anything of that sort is money flow touches anywhere from qualified on-ramps to the company custodies through their end user custodies, right? So you actually wanna mix and match across. So let's take example of a payroll company, like the papago. Or remittance company is pretty similar, but let's start with a payroll company. A payroll company says, hey, I wanna pay out right? So on my end, I have dollars. I want to convert those to digital dollars, right? So I need an on-ramp and an ability to move that from fiat to crypto. Then I want operations on my end to store those digital dollars. So I need some sort of treasury wallets with very meaningful controls, right? And that's where I custody my own funds and that's where Fireblocks plays as well. Then I need an ability to remit that money out to the contractors or employees on the other side of the world very, very quickly. And that's where kind of API operations and Fireblocks has come into play. And then the question is okay how do those employees get paid and answer is you want to spin up non-custodial wallets on their end so that they can log into their PPE or remittance type app and they get and they receive funds there they receive their digital dollars and then that continues into, okay how do you get the digital dollar out. You want to issues a card or you want to off ramp to your PICS in Brazil or UPI in India or anything of that sort. So the full lifecycle for a fintech or a payroll company, a remittance company, or exchange, actually touches all of these, touches anywhere from the on-ramps to direct custody, to qualified custody, to kind of API operations, all the way to self-custody and off-ramp. And what we've seen when we talk to fintechs is they don't want five API end points, your point, or like five different ways of doing this. They want a single unified place to do all of it because they kind of just want to run their business. They care about crypto being effective, an effective tool in running their business, but they don't really care about crypto. It's crypto. Right. And so that's kind of the flow that we see very often. That's awesome. I think it's very clear and great example you just gave. And I think the keyword is actually this life cycle point, because increasingly what we want to see as we're thinking about institutional adoption is it's not just like, oh, let's just do that on-ramp and then forget about everything else. Or just let's just do the last bits of the last mile, right? Because I think for blockchain and crypto to be truly effective, we want them to stay in the ecosystem and to think about their end-to to end flows. And to your point, throughout that journey, there's, like subsets of many different use cases, and therefore the demand for the custody setup is quite different. So I think it's really interesting what you just said. Now, I guess how would you pitch Solano Developer Platform then in front of your institutional clients? What do you think is special around is special around the STP? yeah. So, you know, to your previous point, right? Like when, when we think about talking to any non crypto native company and we talked to them a lot, most of my time has been actually with FinTech and global payroll companies and remittance companies, et cetera, uh, you realize very quickly, they quickly that they want a single, unified solution. They don't want to mix and match. They don't want ten solutions. They don't want to combine different things. They want to come to experts and single sources of truth and do as much as humanly possible through those because at their scale, it's not just even about the technical integration. It's about getting through different security reviews and getting through compliance reviews and going through the hurdles of getting a new vendor onboarded. And so the platform that is being quarterbacked by Solana comes in is, in kind of, in my opinion, a phenomenal, like push in that direction, pushing the direction of kind of a unified face of the crypto industry of saying, here's your single spot in which you can do everything, or which you can explore everything and experience everything. And you don't have to start by figuring out, okay, what do I do for this, and how does this system interact with this system, et cetera? That is the power here. The power is ... I spend a lot of my time talking about, okay, how do cards interact with non-custodial embedded wallets? If that can be abstracted away ... that's a win for everyone. So that is the power of the Salon and the Developer Platform. That's what makes us excited about it. Stacey Spitzer Lathrop-Hood Yeah, definitely. I think we basically think about it as a one-stop shop to your point, right? We have all of these infra ecosystem partners aggregated through this single platform and then we give the flexibility for our client to then pick and choose whatever they want. I guess my last question for you, is also, especially when you were at Dynamic, you've dealt with a lot of the sort of the more crypto native type of enterprises, whether that's Kraken of the world, right? But now, like with Fireblocks, I think you also interact with a lot of the more traditional Web2 type of enterprises, if you will. So I think, in terms of like, the sort of different requirements and what they're looking for from a provider such as Fireblocks plus dynamic, what is the gap? And how do you close that gap? Absolutely. I think that in the business that we're working on, we're abstracting away the complexity of crypto. As Dynamics started, it abstracted away the complexity of extracting away complexity of crypto, right? At Dynamic, it started with abstracting away the complexity of key management, right? We provide an MPC solution, meaning there's no private key. It's behind email login or Google login, right? And so you don't need to think about saving 12 or 24 word seed phrases, right? So we started with that business and abstracting away that complexity. But then when you start thinking about non-crypto companies, you think about, how do you abstract away more complex things like gas, right, and smart contracts? And automation, right? And how do approvals work and how does recovery work, and recovery? And so as you move towards non-crypto companies and you move towards the biggest FinTechs in the world, the same kind of rules apply that they would expect from any other enterprise company that they deal with. How do you think about single sign-on? And how do you think about rules and permissions? And all that type of stuff. Right? How do you think about single sign on? How do you think about rules and permissions? And so over the last couple months in a year or two dynamic, we have really shifted towards a list of here are all the things … and actually, literally today we're doing an internal hackathon dynamic of what else might be confusing and make sense to us because we live and breathe the web 3 but would make sense to know what it's. Right? So we're trying to abstract away as many crypto concepts as possible. So that someone who is a non crypto native developer, which we deal with a lot shop shows up in up in the morning and can build their own version of Venmo or their own version of Armmittance app or their own Neobank Neo Bank by midday. That is what we're going for. And they should be able to do that, just like they would implement Plaid, and be able to interact with entire banking system without needing to know any of the complexity of the entire banking system, right? Or Twilio and be able to integrate and say, I can send SMS or WhatsApp to anywhere in the world within an hour. And Tweleo handles the complexity, I don't need to know anything about how AT&T works, right? It kind of just works. In the same way, we're doing that for crypto, the ability for you to hook up to this Solana-based global financial system without any of the complexity around it. Lin-Yeah, we actually have very similar discussions internally because we want to test how good SDP will be after it's launched. And I'll go, can we buy code of BAMO like kind of app using the APIs we have. So we'll see if we get that, but I think also just, I think was worth mentioning is, everything is entirely API based and we start with everything is also ai native so we have like these stp skills set up ready for users to use so I think this time is going to be quite different in terms of the use experience but also like the product channel how quickly and what kind of product you can get so yeah we'll see so Yitai, thank you so much for being on the podcast with me today. Very fascinating to hear a lot of these cases you just shared and definitely looking forward to partnering with you guys developing SDP-OUT. Same. Thank you for being great partners. We really appreciate it.
